title.narrative: Output 3.5. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement labour market programmes and employment services for transitions to decent work over the life course, with particular focus on young and older workers

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Manpower established the capacity development system for public employment services (PES) staff by developing a training package and having master trainers. The training package on job search assistance and career counselling for PES staff members was developed based on the ILO guidelines; 11 master trainers, consisting of 2 from BPJS and 9 from the Ministry of Manpower were accredited in May 2021. They will act as master trainers for other staff members in the PES.
Linkages between skills development and other labour market policies have been enhanced to generate greater synergies among policy interventions by establishing the Task Force for Cooperation among three DGs of Vocational training, Employment Promotion and Industrial Relation and Social Protection under the Secretary General. The ILO led the design and development of the training package and provided technical inputs. The package was validated by the Ministry of Manpower and tested through a pilot training and further improved.
The ILO and the Ministry of Manpower conducted the training of trainers. The ILO supported the design of the program and participated with a resource specialist.
The ILO suggested and promoted the idea of one-stop service centres where jobseekers can claim unemployment benefit, receive guidance/assistance with job search, and referral to training programmes through policy discussion on Active Labour Market Policy (ALMP) organized in July 2021 in partnership with TEMPO, one of the largest media company. Over 500 members of ILO constituents and the public participated in the event.
The ILO and the University of Indonesia conducted a study on the impact of COVID-19 pandemic on workers. The output will be used to deepen policy debates on job-rich and inclusive recovery from the pandemic in which ALMPs will feature.

description.narrative:
The TVET system designed and implemented on-the-job-training scheme for the graduates of selected TVETs with Employers' Association of Indonesia (APINDO), under a framework of public-private partnership (PPP) which could be regarded as an innovative institutionalized collaboration arrangement between industries and TVET institutions in Indonesia. The following are some of its results:
- Digital/distance learning piloted and promoted to ease access of rural residents, including women and men, to quality training. - On-line pedagogical skills training module for supervisors/ mentor of apprentices developed. - Implemented quality apprenticeship at 20 enterprises, including capacity building on the subject for 10 enterprises.
- Feasibility study with recommendation to promote quality skills development in rural areas through on-line learning developed. - Partnership between maritime companies and HE/TVET institutions strengthened, apprenticeships promoted. Industry engagement will be done through Sector Skill Council (PHRI and AINAKI) (INSIGHT-2). Women in STEM Project partnering with BLK and APINDO to implement digital litercy) In May-August 2020, Women in STEM project conducted online e-commerce training followed by 624 people of which 60% were female. In November 2020-April 2021, the project also conducted Women Digital Development Skill Up training (online web development training) for 683 female students and alumni of vocational education institution, including vocational high schools (SMKs) and TVETs. The training program was conducted together with a representative from ICT industry (Axioo Class Program, ACP) and was deemed up to industry standard. ACP has used the completion of Web development training as a substitute for competency evaluation for software development major in SMKs that collaborate with ACP for the competency exam (Ujian Keahlian Kompetensi, UKK). Insight-2 project corganized national seminar on digital skills and distance learning, series webinar on e-BLK, feasibity study on e-BLK and training on Soft Skill targeting job seekers. INSIGHT-2 Project completed virtual pedagogical training materials for mnetor. Plan to be released in June 2021. Term of Reference for eries webinar and online workshop on apprenticeship is completed and discussed with relevant stakeholders of industry. Fesibilty study on E-BLK has been strated to be undertaken with UT and is expected to be completed by September 2021. This is in progress and on target. We have established four Industry Advisory Boards, linked to each of our four partner polytechnics. To date 24 MOUs have been signed between Industry and TVET institutions.

description.narrative:
The country established a training programme on management/ soft skills for Public Vocational Training Centre (BLKs). Additional results include: - Adopted digital/ distance learning promotion strategy to provide 1,000 access to the online modules. - Published policy recommendation on skills development fund. - Assessment report on digital skills needs in ICT sectors carried out.
- Stakeholders engaged in skills development through the sector skills council. - Showcased innovative skills training for vulnerable communities, in reponse to the COVID-19 pandemic. In June-July 2020 and October - December 2020, the ILO "Women in STEM" project pioneered and conducted 2 batches of online training for 180 TVETs' instructors from 131 TVETs in 28 provinces. INSIGHT-2 Project has undertaken virtual training for isntructors in collaboration with SKILLVUL. For the Women Digital Development Skill Up by Women in STEM Project, Clevio Coder Camp and Axioo Class Program created and used LMS for the delivery of the online training; 683 women completed the minimum training requirement. Insight 2: Digital skills and distance learning strategy will be developed based on feasibility study INSIGHT-2 project developed a policy brief on skills development fund. In April 2021, Women in STEM project concluded a research project looking at the needs for ICT related skills in Indonesian SMEs including those in ICT industry. Insight 2: Rapid Assessment on ITC Sector skills demand report has been completed and diseminated. The report has been published and and disseminated through social media (In collabraiton with GRID Network).
1,650 young people, women, rural residents, including people with disabilities, PLHIV and Refugees were trained on various skills fro livelihood and employment. It is expected that at least 10% of the participants will secure a decent job.

description.narrative: Three public training centers developed systematic coordination and collaboration with industries located in their area to design and deliver ICT related trainings that meet industry needs with a focus on women. The Ministry of Manpower and public training centers enhanced the responsiveness of the skills development system to changing skills demand, especially digital skills, through stronger industry-TVET collaboration. Results include: - Developed guide for developing national competency standard (SKKNI). - Implemented twenty memorandums of understanding between Public Vocational Training Centres (BLK) and local enterprises (TVET-Industry Collaboration). - Piloted two new digital skills training curriculum and programme schemes with public training centers. - Developed an assessment tool for public vocational training centres (BLKs). - Developed and piloted re-skilling training courses and material with the public training centers. - Developed a sector skills/workforce development strategy for the maritime sector in coordination with the industry growth/transformation plan. Between November 2020 and April 2021, the ILO project “Women in STEM”, together with Clevio Coder Camp and a representative from ICT industry, Axioo Class Program, conducted the Women Digital Development Skill Up training (online) for 683 female students and alumni of vocational education institutions. Six instructors from TVET institutions co-facilitated the training and acted as online coaches. The ILO INSIGHT/ UNIQLO Project supported the development of two digital courses on animation and computer network. Women in STEM also provided computer literacy courses and soft skills for instructors. The ILO also provided technical assistance to the National TVET Committee, coordinated a formal response to the TVET White Paper and facilitated a high level policy exchange event, supported the development of the Sector Skills Council and collaborated in a feasibility study for e-BLK transformation. In addition, the INSIGHT-/ UNIQLO project engaged the industrial sector in developing digital skills vocational training for BBLKI Bekasi and completed virtual training materials for mentor on apprenticeship programme involving KADIN and relevant industry sector.
